Container.Name: NPMpro
Container.Overview:
NPMpro is a reverse proxy with a web UI: add your domains, point them at your services and get HTTPS certificates, without writing nginx configs. It is a hardened fork of Nginx Proxy Manager with HTTP/3, CrowdSec, OIDC sign-in, traffic statistics and backups, in one image.
The web UI is https on port 81. HTTP and HTTPS are mapped to the ports 8080 and 8443, so they do not clash with the Unraid web UI: forward the ports 80 and 443 of your router to 8080 and 8443 of this server. HTTPS uses tcp and udp (HTTP/3).
For the real ports 80 and 443 and client IPs without NAT, set Network Type to br0 (or another custom network) with its own IP: the port mappings then do not apply.
Advanced: COOKIE_SECRET keeps users signed in across restarts. A secret can also come from a file in the secrets folder (set the value or its _FILE variable, never both). Installation guide: https://github.com/TheBlackBush/NPMpro/wiki/Installation-on-Unraid

Config.Name: HTTP port
Config.Description: HTTP for your hosts and the Let's Encrypt HTTP challenge: forward port 80 of your router here.

Config.Name: HTTPS port
Config.Description: HTTPS for your hosts: forward port 443 (tcp) of your router here.

Config.Name: HTTP/3 port
Config.Description: HTTP/3 (QUIC) for your hosts: the same port as HTTPS, over udp; forward port 443 (udp) of your router here.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: All NPMpro data: database, certificates, configs and logs.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User id NPMpro runs as (99 is nobody on Unraid). Set PUID and PGID together.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group id NPMpro runs as (100 is users on Unraid). Set PUID and PGID together.

Config.Name: COOKIE_SECRET
Config.Description: Signs the session cookie: a long random value (openssl rand -hex 32). Empty: a new one at every start, which signs everyone out. Set this or COOKIE_SECRET_FILE, not both.

Config.Name: COOKIE_SECRET_FILE
Config.Description: COOKIE_SECRET from a file instead, such as /run/secrets/cookie_secret (in the secrets folder below).

Config.Name: INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL
Config.Description: Email of the first admin, first start only, with INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD; empty: the setup page creates the first user. Set this or INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL_FILE, not both.

Config.Name: INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL_FILE
Config.Description: INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL from a file instead, such as /run/secrets/initial_admin_email.

Config.Name: INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD
Config.Description: Password of the first admin (8 to 255 characters), first start only, with INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL. Set this or INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE, not both.

Config.Name: INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE
Config.Description: INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD from a file instead, such as /run/secrets/initial_admin_password.

Config.Name: Secrets folder
Config.Description: Optional host folder with the files of the _FILE variables, read-only; keep it outside the appdata folder, files owned by root (mode 600 or 400).
